Inspect or clear the native selection cache

Source: R/selection-cache.R
selection_cache_info.Rd

Reports the bounded native selection-normalizer cache in the current R process. Exact caching reuses identical numerical inputs and does not change the likelihood or its integration diagnostics. Post-fit requests using bounded CDF interpolation bypass these caches, including when they fall back to the ordinary primitive. Fitting retains its ordinary-primitive cache.

Usage

selection_cache_info(clear = FALSE, component = c("all", "exact", "coarse"))

Arguments

clear

clear the requested entries and reset their counters before reporting them. Clearing "all" also releases the shared storage.

component

report the "exact" cache, the "coarse" proposal cache, or "all" caches.

Value

A data frame with the cache component, byte counts, entry count, and lookup, eviction and allocation counters. The "total" row reports the shared capacity and directly allocated blocks, including retained controls and index buckets; component byte counts are NA because storage is shared. Allocator metadata, the surrounding R process and JAGS model are excluded; this is not a process-RSS limit. Eviction releases entry blocks, while controls and index buckets can remain allocated. Oversize lookup keys increment misses without incrementing allocation failures. Failed insertion, capacity or allocation attempts can increment allocation failures; these counts do not necessarily indicate exhaustion of system memory.

Details

The default selection.cache_max_bytes = "auto" chooses the smaller of 4 GiB and one quarter of currently available system RAM. Available RAM is reported by ps::ps_system_memory(), excluding swap. A numeric setting supplies an explicit total byte budget; 0 disables storage. If the available-memory query fails, a warning is issued and caching stays disabled until a budget can be resolved or supplied explicitly. Loading the package does not query available memory. The first selection computation or cache inspection initializes the current process's cache, including computations on a saved fit. Explicit option changes and fitting setup also initialize it. Exact and coarse entries share one byte budget for directly allocated key, control, list-node and index blocks, with global least-recently-used eviction. Storage is allocated lazily. The ordinary sampler does not use coarse entries.

The budget is resolved once before fitting and divided equally among chains. Shares are pooled for chains assigned to the same process: ten parallel workers receive one tenth each, while ten sequential chains share the total. Integer-byte rounding can leave a few bytes unused. The coordinator releases its cache while workers run and restores its local budget when they stop. Separate simultaneous fits are separate budgets; this is not a machine-wide memory manager. Stored fit extensions retain the resolved budget and sampler settings, redistributing the budget for their current worker topology.

This function reports only the current process, not separate workers or saved fitted-object caches. By default entries live in the native process. Set RoBMA.options(selection.cache_retain = TRUE) to retain them with the fit; see remove_selection_cache. Changing the budget or clearing all entries releases the shared storage. Clearing one component releases its keys, nodes and controls; shared index buckets can remain allocated. Switching sampler options does not clear existing entries or replace already compiled samplers.

The exact cache accelerates successful deterministic covariance-envelope normalizers for multivariate step selection. Unsupported numerical routes continue through their ordinary evaluator. The coarse cache can also store its prescribed unit-normalizer fallback. If cache storage cannot be allocated, the same exact or surrogate evaluator runs without storage; memory capacity never determines the returned normalizer or its numerical diagnostics.
